legend.expected_class: DEFAULT | IMPORTANT_I | IMPORTANT_II | CRITICAL | UNRESOLVED | NOT_ASSERTED
legend.NOT_ASSERTED: The case tests engine behaviour rather than this outcome. A comparison must treat NOT_ASSERTED as 'no claim', never as a disagreement.
legend.expected_category: For per-category pairs only: which category, and whether it should match.

status: Statuses follow DR-04. AUTHOR_VERIFIED means the conditions trace verbatim to official text we hold; AUTHOR_INTERPRETATION means our reading goes beyond the literal text; OPEN_QUESTION means the law is undetermined and the engine must not resolve it. No status asserts legal endorsement.

cases.scenario: Component for a type-approved motor vehicle
cases.expected_behaviour: Art. 2(2)(c) exclusion where that Regulation applies to the product
cases.contested: We keep OUT, but the reviewer's caution is reasonable: whether Reg. 2019/2144 applies to a component rather than the vehicle should be confirmed.
cases.review_change: Round 2: Reg. (EU) 2019/2144 Art. 2 expressly covers systems, components and separate technical units for vehicle categories M, N and O, and the Commission guidance (s.9.3.1) distinguishes components EXCLUSIVELY designed and constructed for covered vehicles (excluded) from generic components that merely can be integrated (not excluded). Our scenario establishes only use in a type-approved vehicle, not exclusivity. Changed from OUT to UNRESOLVED.

cases.scenario: Exclusion claimed but applicable instrument unidentified
cases.expected_behaviour: No exclusion granted; question returned
cases.review_change: Reviewer correction, accepted: where the basis for a claimed exclusion is UNKNOWN, scope is UNRESOLVED. Treating it as IN converts an UNKNOWN into a FALSE, which is the thing our own four-valued model forbids.

cases.scenario: Avionics product within scope of Reg. 2018/1139 but not certified under it
cases.expected_behaviour: Art. 2(3) excludes only products *certified in accordance with* 2018/1139 — scope alone is not enough

cases.scenario: Sectoral rules claimed to cover the Annex I risks
cases.expected_behaviour: No exclusion unless a delegated act under Art. 2(5) actually says so; absence of an act is not an exclusion
cases.contested: We keep IN. Art. 2(5) requires a delegated act for the limitation to exist; the absence of one is determinable, not unknown, so this is not the EXC-06 situation.
cases.review_change: Round 2 confirms IN where no applicable exclusion instrument exists - but corrects the reasoning. The engine must check for an APPLICABLE delegated act under Art. 2(5), not whether any delegated act exists. See the claim about Delegated Reg. (EU) 2025/1535 in docs/legal/sources/MANIFEST.md, which is UNVERIFIED.
